contradictions.detail: The dealer's walkaround video claims a 'clean Carfax', but the Carfax reports an accident on 01/16/2009. Autotrader's own history badge also says 'Accident or Damage Reported'.
The description says 'only 46,381 miles', while the header and Carfax say 46,516. This is most likely a stale description, since the 9/30/2026 reading was 46,396.
The description calls it a 'roadster', 'convertible' and 'open-top design', but the photos, VIN and TrueCar all show a hardtop coupe.

critical_evidence.evidence: No photos of the underside, rear subframe or diff mount, and no trunk floor shown with the carpet lifted. The trunk carpet and spare well look dry and rust-free. The coupe body is stiffer, but subframe-mount cracking still has to be checked, especially with a repaired passenger rear quarter nearby.

Carfax documents coolant flushes in 4/2005, 1/2008, 7/2012 and 12/2019. There is no reported entry for a water pump, thermostat, radiator or expansion tank. The tank looks original/yellowed in the video. One thermostat-housing hose looks fresh but has no invoice. Component ages are unproven on a 25-year-old system.

documentation.rationale: Both halves are present. Identity and terms: VIN, itemised price ($25,715 + $989 fee) and a Carfax with title, owner and accident data. Maintenance: about 30 dated service entries including coolant and brake fluid, a 2026 PDI invoice line list, paint-depth readings and extra photos. Missing: any repair documentation for the 2009 accident, and photos of the underside and subframe.

condition.rationale: Documented positives: new tires, alignment, timing-chain tensioner/guide, filters and oil (10/2026); dry, clean engine bay; uncracked dash; good leather. Observed negatives: a heavily refinished passenger rear quarter (14–19 mils) from the reported 2009 accident; corrosion and a possible blister at the hatch-handle trim edge; hood scratch; hazy headlights; pitted chrome trim. Underside and subframe were not examined.

price_value.rationale: $26,704 sits at the fair-value mid ($26,520) for clean coupes. This car carries a reported accident and a refinished quarter, which comps discount. The one silver/black repaired-collision coupe brought $25,250 hammer at 79k. Cosmetic known work pulls this down further.

mission_fit.rationale: Factory manual and a fixed-roof coupe, so the roof and rain concern is better than any roadster. The car is available now, with one long-term owner, and sits inside the $27,000 ceiling but above the ideal band. The reported accident is a heavy penalty under Jason's history rules, and a 25-year-old BMW carries higher running costs than an RF.

logistics.rationale: The car is in Fredericksburg VA, so Jason would fly out and drive home cross-country. The dealer explicitly invites an independent mobile inspector before purchase. Virginia emissions passed and California registration looks feasible.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Several desirable traits together: a rare 3.0i coupe body, a manual, one owner for 25 years, mostly stock, with sunroof, heated seats and Harman/Kardon. Silver over black is common rather than special, and the Kenwood head unit is a minor deviation.

positives: Carfax confirms one personal owner from new in 2001 to 2026, with about 30 service records, almost all at BMW of Charlottesville, and a consistent mileage trail to 46,516.
Rare factory-manual 3.0i coupe: a fixed roof suits year-round rain use better than any roadster.
Fresh 10/2026 dealer work on the Carfax: four tires, alignment, timing-chain tensioner/guide, front rotors resurfaced, filters, oil, Virginia safety and emissions pass.
Clean title, no structural damage, no airbag deployment, no total loss and no open recalls reported. Mostly stock.
Unusually cooperative dealer: walkaround video, paint-depth readings and extra photos, plus an invitation to an independent inspector.
concerns: Observed: Carfax accident 01/16/2009 with no repair record. Paint readings of 14–19 mils on the passenger rear quarter indicate a heavy refinish, possibly with filler. The dealer's verbal 'clean Carfax' claim is wrong.
Observed: white crusty corrosion and a yellow-orange stain at the paint seam under the hatch-handle chrome strip, with a possible blister start. Also a hood scratch, hazy headlights and pitted trim.
Unverified: rear subframe, diff mount and trunk-floor spot welds, especially near the repaired passenger quarter (ask for underside and trunk-floor photos; inspect at the PPI).
Unverified: cooling system component age. Flushes are documented but there is no reported water pump, thermostat or radiator replacement, and the expansion tank looks original (ask for invoices).
Unverified: no reported brake-fluid service since 2012, and very low use since 2016. Seals, bushings and VANOS should be checked on a car that has sat (ask for records).
Unverified: why the timing-chain tensioner/guide was replaced at the PDI (ask whether there was a rattle or noise).

ppi_focus: Passenger rear quarter: paint-depth survey, filler check with a magnet, panel gaps, and the inner structure and wheel-well seams behind the 2009 repair
Rear subframe mounts, diff ears and trunk-floor spot welds, with photos from below and from the trunk
Hatch-handle area and hatch lower edge: probe the corrosion and blister at the chrome-strip seam
Cooling system: pressure test, inspect the expansion tank neck, water pump play, radiator end tanks and fan clutch
Cold start: VANOS rattle, timing-chain noise after the new tensioner, DISA valve rattle
Valve cover and oil filter housing gaskets, oil pan and rear main for seepage after long low-use periods
Brake fluid moisture test and caliper slide condition, given 14 years with no reported flush
Rear trailing-arm and front control-arm bushings, and clutch engagement point and slip
Sunroof seals and drains, hatch seal, and door seals for water ingress (a year-round rain car)
OBD scan for stored codes, readiness monitors for California smog, and cluster warning lights
what_would_change_verdict: Up: underside, subframe and trunk-floor photos or a PPI showing a sound structure, plus a repair record showing the 2009 accident was cosmetic and confined to the quarter.
Up: the dealer removing the $989 fee or cutting the price to reflect the accident discount.
Up: invoices showing the water pump, thermostat and radiator were done within roughly the last 30k miles or 8 years.
Down: filler, kinked seams or misalignment at the passenger rear quarter or inner structure, or any subframe cracking.
Down: active corrosion spreading under the hatch paint, or a cold-start rattle persisting after the tensioner job.
evidence.mission_note: A factory-manual, fixed-roof Z3 3.0i coupe with one long-term owner fits the year-round enthusiast-bridge brief well and is resaleable within 6–24 months. The reported accident and refinished quarter weigh against it under Jason's history rules, and the asking price is in the upper band, above the ideal range.
evidence.rationale: The Carfax establishes one personal owner from 2001 to 2026 and a clean title. Its roughly 30 dealer service entries, including coolant flushes through 2019 and brake fluid through 2012, give a consistent mileage trail to 46,516. The same report records an accident on 01/16/2009 with no severity or repair record. The seller's paint-depth readings (14–19 mils on the passenger rear quarter against about 4–7.5 elsewhere) place a heavy refinish there, which contradicts the dealer's verbal 'clean Carfax'. Observed defects are cosmetic but real: corrosion and a possible blister at the hatch-handle trim seam, a hood scratch, hazy headlights and pitted trim. Fresh dealer work in 10/2026 covers tires, alignment, the timing-chain tensioner/guide, filters and a Virginia emissions pass. Still open: rear subframe and trunk-floor condition, cooling-component ages, brake fluid since 2012, and the reason for the tensioner replacement. At $26,704 the car sits at the clean-coupe fair-value mid despite the accident history, which comps discount.
evidence.next_action: Ask the dealer for the 2009 accident repair record, the 9/30/2026 and PDI invoices, and lift photos of the rear subframe and trunk floor. Then book a mobile PPI at Pohanka focused on the passenger rear quarter, the subframe and the cooling system.

provenance.summary: The most consequential finding is that the body style is described inconsistently. The VIN prefix and TrueCar indicate a Z3 Coupe 3.0i, yet the dealer copy calls the car an 'open-top' convertible and the dealer site title calls it a 'Sedan'. The buyer should confirm the body in person, since coupes and roadsters are valued differently. The dealer's own description gives 46,381 miles while the listing shows 46,516; that 135-mile gap may reflect use while in stock or stale copy. An aggregator recorded an October 2026 asking price of $26,964, against the current $26,704 (which includes a $989 'not required by law' processing fee), suggesting a modest $260 reduction. No auction results, prior private-sale listings or forum discussions are tied to this VIN; the 'CARFAX 1-Owner' claim is the dealer's own and should be checked against the report. Two 47k-mile Bring a Trailer Z3 3.0i postings seen on Facebook, one specifically a Coupe 5-speed, are worth checking by VIN, because a recent public auction sale would undercut the one-owner claim and reveal a prior sale price.
